extracted.intended_audience: educated readers and students of natural philosophy, biology, sociology, and the arts
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and explicating the many forms of 'integration' (coalescence, consolidation, mutual dependence) that the author presents as the universal process of evolutionary progress across organisms, societies, language, science, and the arts. Focuses on both primary integration (coherence) and secondary redistributions (division into parts / compound evolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Longitudinal integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration occurring along the length of an organism — reduction in number of segments and consolidation of parts into compact units (e.g., in Annulosa: many-segmented worms/myriapods -> crustaceans, insects, spiders with fewer segments; in vertebrates: fusion of vertebrae forming sacrum and coccyx).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and developmental parallels: embryonic segments that were separable become united (lobster head + thorax forming a compact box; butterfly segments less distinguishable than in caterpillar). Use as evidence linking ontogeny and phylogeny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transverse integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration occurring across the body (crosswise), illustrated by fusion/union of paired structures into single medial structures (e.g., nervous system ganglia consolidation in Annulosa; coalescence of cephalic ganglia into a brain; generative system ducts converging in mammals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed examples: in Astacus (crayfish) pairs of ganglia unite progressively into single masses; in Vertebrata ovarian/uterine ducts show convergence from separate lateral organs to more coalesced forms in higher mammals. Shows simultaneous longitudinal and transverse integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organic integrations within same species (gregarious/combination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms of integration by which organisms of the same species become dependent/combined (from simple aggregation to cooperative bodies): pack hunting, sentinel systems, leadership, polygamous family groupings, social insects where individuals cannot survive separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree varies from simple aggregation to highly consolidated social insects; indicates increasing mutual dependence among conspecifics as part of evolutionary integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organic integrations among different species (interdependence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrations that make different species dependent on one another: food chains (animals living on plants; carnivores needing herbivores), plant–insect mutualisms (pollination), habitat-specific interdependencies where species die out when transplanted away from coexisting flora/fauna.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Darwin's illustrations; emphasizes that flora and fauna of a habitat form an integrated aggregate that increases in integration with organic evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Super-organic integration (societal aggregation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregative processes among human groups: families -> tribes -> subjugated/combined tribes -> principalities -> kingdoms -> potential federations; progressive unification and increased stability of larger social wholes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: formation of tribes from wandering families, subordination of chiefs, formation of feudal aggregates, growth of centralized power (dukes/earls -> king), and tendencies toward international federation via alliances, congresses, breakdown of barriers, improved communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal social integration: regulative vs operative unions
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishes two internal orders of social unions as societies organize: regulative (governmental, administrative, military, ecclesiastical, legal classes — caste-like separations) and operative (industrial/occupational organizations producing physical approach and co-location).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulative classes are bound by privileges, blood, education; operative integrations are direct and physical (growth of industrial centres, concentration of trades, municipal agglomerations). Examples include Manchester with weaving suburbs, centralization of publishers at Paternoster Row, bank and railway clearing-houses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial/operative integrations (concentration and centralization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrations arising from economic/industrial organization that produce physical concentration of functions: one place monopolizing production, centers attracting masters and workers, concentration of trades in particular city districts, factories uniting many machines under one power source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Yorkshire cloth-districts displacing other centres, Staffordshire absorbing pottery manufacture, concentration of publishers, bankers, engineers; modern factories where many machines are united by a single steam engine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration in language (agglutination -> amalgamation -> analytic forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Progressive unification of language elements: compounding and agglutination in primitive tongues leading to fusion of syllables, loss of inflections, contraction of polysyllables into mono-/dissyllables, and development from aptotic (isolating) to agglutinate to amalgamate to analytic ('anaptotic') languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: North American languages with long compounds vs English monosyllables; Anglo-Saxon steorra -> English star, mona -> moon; loss of terminal inflections (cuman -> come); Chinese as an example of aptotic/isolating language; frequency of repetition speeds fusion (e.g., Good bye from God be with you).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammatical integration producing sentence coherence and complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: As inflections coalesce and connective mechanisms evolve, language permits stronger binding of sentence elements into complex, interdependent structures: subordinate propositions, complements, and qualifying clauses produce complex, non-interchangeable sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast Hebrew scriptures (simpler aggregation) with modern compositions (many subordinate clauses); increasing grammatical integration correlates with capacity for complex thought and expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration in science (classification, generalization, colligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific progress is integration: arranging objects and relations into groups and higher generalizations; uniting previously separate orders of phenomena under common laws (classification of organisms, colligation of relations into generalizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: zoology's Vertebrata, Annulosa, etc.; Humboldt's linking of light and sound phenomena; recent integration of Electricity, Magnetism, and Light; scientific advance seen as growth of nested, mutually-dependent generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration in industrial and aesthetic arts (unity and subordination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress from simple tools to complex machines and from dispersed pictorial elements to unified compositions; merit judged by subordination of parts to the whole and success in producing a coherent total effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanical examples: lever -> wheel-and-axle -> modern machines composed of many primitive machines; artistic examples: contrast Egyptian/Assyrian mural dispersal with modern historical painting's coordinated composition; measure of merit = unity from variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration in music (melodic, harmonic, orchestral cohesion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Music shows progressive integration from simple repeated cadences to elaborate melismatic and harmonic structures: melody + bass + tenor + alto + accompaniment + orchestral/choreographic combination into musical drama, where artistic perfection largely consists in subordination of particulars to total effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integration stages: simple cadence -> combined musical phrases -> multi-part harmony -> orchestral ensemble -> musical drama; missing final notes or interrupting integrated melody produces painful incompleteness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration in literature and drama (causal unity and character interdependence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primitive tales are loose sequences of unrelated adventures; good modern imaginative works exhibit events as consequences of character actions under conditions, with characters mutually modifying minds and acting through consistent moral relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure of narrative integration: events cannot be arbitrarily reordered without harming effect; characters' interactions and psychological coherence indicate higher integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary definition of evolution as increased coherence via dissipation of motion and integration of matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolution (primary aspect) defined as change from less coherent form to more coherent form, consequent on dissipation of motion and integration of matter, occurring universally across solar systems, organisms, nations, and social products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This universal process manifests as aggregation of mass, increase in density, loss of relative motion, consolidation of parts into cooperative assemblages; applies equally to celestial, organic, and super-organic phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual dependence and specialization as indicators of degree of development
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of development/integration measured by mutual dependence of parts (e.g., organisms unable to lose parts without dying; societies with highly coordinated parts; sciences and divisions mutually dependent for investigation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast organisms that regenerate when cut vs those that die if parts are removed; social products (sciences) become highly integrated when divisions cannot operate without aid from others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound evolution and secondary redistributions (structural modification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond primary integration, evolution includes secondary redistributions of matter and motion causing a whole to divide into parts and produce persistent structural modifications; this 'compound evolution' addresses how wholes come to be partitioned into specialized parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secondary redistributions produce evanescent results in very incoherent aggregates but persistent structural changes in aggregates of medium coherence; raises the question of a universal expression for these structural modifications (preview of further analysis).
